system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**From:** AI legal assistant (buyer side)
**Status:** Preliminary review against the Buyer Negotiation Playbook. Not for transmission to the Seller.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" assertion

The Seller's preamble says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "marked FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened". **We have no record supporting this.** Our playbook is explicit that the 20% cap and the 18-month claims period are fallbacks usable *only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and **none has been given**. The Seller's "market context" paragraph is advocacy, not evidence of agreement, and it should not be allowed to anchor our response.

**Recommendation:** Before anything else, confirm internally with Amelia Frost that no principal-level concession has been made. Assuming none, respond that the Seller's draft does not reflect any agreed position and that all limitation terms are open and will be marked up in full. Do not accept "FINAL" labels on a counterparty draft.

---

## 1. Liability regime (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

| Item | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (20% only with Frost authority — none) | **Reject.** Revert to 25%. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5× our position. Revert. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, **excess only** (deductible) | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar** (tipping) | 5× our figure *and* wrong mechanic. Both must change. |
| Claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval — none) | Revert to 24 months. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Critical departure.** Flatly reject. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13) | Default general-regime override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden override | Reject. This clause silently sweeps Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into the general cap and 18 months. |
| 9.3/12.8/20.5 limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" | No carve-outs | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of *everything*; specific indemnities and covenants outside exclusive remedy | **Critical.** There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's draft. This is non-negotiable for us and the playbook says no one may waive it. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion for anything Buyer *or its advisers* knew *or could have discovered* from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Note it is a *constructive* knowledge test ("discoverable"), which combined with the general data-room disclosure (below) would effectively nullify the warranties. |

**Reasoning.** Taken together, Clauses 8.3, 12, 13 and Schedule 7 produce a package where (i) almost every matter is deemed disclosed, (ii) almost every matter is deemed known, (iii) what survives is capped at 20%, subject to a 1% deductible, and time-barred at 18 months, and (iv) title, capacity, tax, IP and even fraud sit inside the same box. Each piece is individually off-playbook; the combined effect is that the warranty package provides very little real protection. We should resist the Seller's framing of these as separate "administrative" points and respond on the package as a whole.

**Recommendations:**
- Revert all numbers to playbook (25% / AUD 6m; AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket; 24 months).
- Insert a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price, 6 years minimum, outside de minimis, basket and knowledge qualification.
- Insert an express, unwaivable carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- Delete the "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default; replace with express drafting that specific indemnities, covenants, Tax and IP claims sit in their own categories.
- Delete 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier survives, it must be actual knowledge of named buyer deal-team individuals, with no "discoverable" limb, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

---

## 2. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1)

The Seller discloses the *entire* data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" generally. Playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Para 1.4 ("nothing in this letter admits ... that any consent, payment, notice ... is legally required") is a standard non-admission, but combined with the general disclosure it means the Seller is simultaneously (a) relying on the data room to disclose against warranties and (b) declining to characterise what the documents mean.

**Recommendation:** Reject §1.1 and §1.2. Require specific disclosures referenced to the warranty being qualified, with a "fair disclosure" standard (sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). General disclosure of public registers to be limited, if at all, to ASIC company searches of the Company itself as at a fixed date.

---

## 3. Bluefen consent (Clause 3 / 6.3)

**Seller position:** reasonable endeavours; consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
**Disclosure Letter §2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); DD-002 cl 11.2 consent with conditions in cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied** as at the letter date.

**Why this matters:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue. "Consent on delivery" means a conditional consent (e.g. subject to pricing, SLA or guarantee conditions under cl 11.3) would satisfy the condition precedent even if the conditions never bite. Reasonable endeavours is too weak for a material customer.

**Recommendation:** Condition precedent requires (i) an **effective, unconditional** written consent from Bluefen (or consent whose cl 11.3 conditions are evidenced as satisfied) **before Completion**, (ii) Seller to use all reasonable endeavours with a cooperation covenant and Buyer approval over any concession offered to Bluefen, and (iii) a Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within a defined period post-Completion on account of the change of control.

---

## 4. Riverlark facility (Clause 2 / 7)

**Seller position:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter §3:** facility not repaid; no final discharge; change-of-control under cl 8.1.

**Why this matters:** We are buying debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means we acquire a company that is in change-of-control default under cl 8.1 at the moment of Completion, with security over the business, and rely on the Seller/Riverlark to tidy up afterwards.

**Recommendation:** Require (i) a payout letter from Riverlark current to the Completion date, (ii) direct repayment of the payout figure from Completion funds (deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics), and (iii) executed security releases/PPSR discharge documents delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and **Amelia Frost approval** — not currently given.

---

## 5. Employee bonuses — DD-005 (Funds flow)

**Seller position:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure Letter §5:** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not** in the draft funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Why this matters:** The bonuses are triggered by *our* Completion and will be paid by *the Company* (i.e. us) unless funded. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company bears AUD 420,000 plus on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, potentially leave accruals) post-Completion — in substance a price increase.

**Recommendation:** Either (a) a specific line item in the funds flow deducting AUD 420,000 **plus** grossed-up on-costs from the price / treated as Debt, or (b) a Seller covenant to fund the gross amount to the Company at Completion, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general cap. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in the Disclosure Letter.

---

## 6. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)

**Seller position:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Disclosure Letter §4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room; the AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified.

**Why this matters:** If any SOW3 fee is unpaid, title to the Project Materials has not passed. The risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is the ownership of IP that may sit in the product. An indemnity for the payment alone does not cover loss of IP, third-party claims or the cost of re-procurement.

**Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or encumbrance over the SOW3 Project Materials (and any other Ironquay deliverables), outside the general cap and basket. Preserve the SOW3 cure: Seller to procure, at its cost before Completion, (i) payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees, (ii) Ironquay's written receipt, and (iii) a confirmatory assignment. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as established either way — require bank evidence.

---

## 7. Export/privacy incident — DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)

**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter §6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary; no loss figure.

**Assessment:** Per playbook, assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** in either direction. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a characterisation it has not substantiated; equally we should not overstate it. The gap is informational.

**Recommendation:** Require (i) a preservation covenant for all logs and link-access records, (ii) a proper investigation to be completed (or at least a defined report) before Completion, (iii) ongoing updates and Buyer access to the investigation, (iv) a specific warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is complete as at Completion, and (v) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sized once facts are known. Reject any attempt to have DD-006 "disclosed" generally against the data-protection warranties.

---

## 8. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

**Seller position:** ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter §8:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008 / DD-011, read together for timing/scope); the letter does **not** state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Assessment:** Playbook says assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. The Seller's "ordinary course" label is not supported by its own disclosure, which expressly declines to characterise them.

**Recommendation:** Ask DD questions: renewal dates, termination rights, whether services are needed post-Completion, whether any amounts are accrued or prepaid at the Locked Box/Completion date. Hold open the possibility of treating any pre-Completion accrued or non-terminable amounts as Debt or working-capital items, but do not assert a deduction yet.

---

## 9. Tax / IP warranties

**Seller position:** "settled under the general regime above".
**Playbook:** OPEN; keep separate categories; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

**Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation as settled. Tax and IP warranties to be addressed in their own schedules with their own cap and time-limit regime (to be negotiated). Do not accept their absorption into the 20% / 18-month general regime by default.

---

## 10. Title

**Seller position:** title to 100% of shares "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012".
**Disclosure Letter §10:** this is the source the Seller relies on; does not state that the Buyer has verified it.

**Assessment:** DD-012 is an internal, Seller-supplied document. It is not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances, or Harbourglass's authority to sell.

**Recommendation:** Require (i) current ASIC company search, (ii) PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, (iii) Harbourglass board resolutions and constitutional authority to sell, (iv) share certificates or confirmation none issued, and (v) a fundamental warranty on title, capacity and no encumbrances under the separate Fundamental regime (item 1). Also confirm the Riverlark security (item 4) does not extend to the shares themselves.

---

## 11. Lesser points for completeness

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, not consent — accept but include a Seller covenant to give the notice pre-Completion and evidence it.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction does not bite on a share sale per the disclosure. Verify the clause ourselves (change-of-control vs assignment language); if confirmed, no action.
- **Disclosure Letter §11 (Reservation):** harmless, but note the Seller itself says we must evaluate the facts against the "complete agreement and current due diligence record" — which cuts against its own "FINAL" preamble.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Reject the "FINAL / principal-level" framing.** Confirm internally that no Frost authority exists; respond that all limitation terms are open.
2. **Liability regime back to playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket; 24 months.
3. **Separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100%, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge bar. Reject the "administrative simplicity" merger.
4. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
5. **Delete Clause 8.3** buyer-knowledge exclusion and the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default in 12.3/13.
6. **Specific fair disclosure only;** reject data-room, register and public-record general disclosure.
7. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of cl 11.3 condition satisfaction as a pre-Completion CP; not consent-on-delivery.
8. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.
9. **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with specific indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity to loss of IP title; require pre-Completion cure and confirmatory assignment; verify the AUD 180k independently.
11. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no characterisation either way.
12. **Sandbar:** DD questions; no deduction asserted yet.
13. **Tax / IP:** remain open in separate schedules.
14. **Title:** independent searches and authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.

If helpful, I can turn this into a numbered issues list in the Seller's clause order for the formal mark-up, or draft the covering response rejecting the "FINAL" characterisation.
=== END ADVICE ===
